steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Nature vs nurture: nature argues behaviour is determined by inherited genes and biology; nurture argues behaviour is determined by experience and environment. Modern view: interactionism - both contribute. Epigenetics shows environmental factors can switch genes on/off, demonstrating that nature and nurture interact.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Free will vs determinism: free will argues people have conscious control over their choices; determinism argues behaviour is caused by factors beyond our control. Biological determinism (genes/neurochemistry), environmental determinism (conditioning), and psychic determinism (unconscious drives). Soft determinism (Bandura): some freedom within determined constraints.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Reductionism vs holism: reductionism explains behaviour by breaking it down into simpler components (biological reductionism: behaviour = brain chemistry). Holism argues the whole is greater than the sum of parts - behaviour must be understood as an integrated system. Reductionism is scientific but oversimplifies; holism is comprehensive but harder to test.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethnocentrism: judging other cultures by the standards of your own. Much research is WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialised, Rich, Democratic) and may not generalise. Example: Asch's conformity findings reflect 1950s America; collectivist cultures show higher conformity.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the nature-nurture debate and evaluate whether behaviour is determined by nature or nurture. | Describe the difference between free will and determinism, giving examples of each from psychological research. | Evaluate whether psychological research suffers from ethnocentric and gender bias, and explain how this can be addressed.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Nature = biology. Nurture = experience. Modern answer: BOTH (interactionism, epigenetics). Free will = we choose. Determinism = behaviour is caused. Soft determinism = influenced but not rigidly fixed. Reductionism = break it down (scientific but oversimplified). Holism = see the whole picture (comprehensive but harder to test).
